summary.headline: Swiggy guides Quick Commerce contribution margin to 0 to -100 bps for growth, with 4-week cumulative NOV growth at 10% vs 1% prior.
summary.overview: Swiggy's Q1 FY27 call (held July 30, 2026) centred on a deliberate pivot from contribution-margin protection to growth in Quick Commerce (Instamart). Management said it reached contribution margin breakeven, closing the last quarter at -0.2%, and now guides to a 0 to -100 bps range to fund store expansion, speed, serviceability and assortment. Take-rate gains were attributed to brand monetisation, advertising and user-fee changes, with management calling them sustainable. Food delivery growth was about 18% adjusted for cancellations, with 18-20% YoY guidance maintained, and management dismissed zero-commission competition from Toing's rivals as unsustainable. Toing, the new value-led food platform, is loss-making and was a major focus, with a Capital Markets Day planned for the following week.

segments.name: Quick Commerce (Instamart)
segments.commentary: Contribution margin reached breakeven, last closed at -0.2%, with guidance of 0 to -100 bps. Plans to add more stores this quarter than in the last four quarters, all in existing cities; network utilisation about 40%.

segments.name: Food Delivery
segments.commentary: Adjusted growth about 18% YoY; YoY guidance 18-20% maintained. Take rate about 3%, with a target of 5%; management expects steady margin accretion.

segments.name: Platform Innovation (Toing, Snacc closed)
segments.commentary: Losses increased, mainly from Toing marketing to acquire users; Snacc closure last quarter left some residual operating costs. Roughly one-third of Toing users are existing Swiggy users. Toing is excluded from B2C GOV reporting.

guidance_outlook: Quick Commerce contribution margin guided to a range of 0 to -100 bps, assuming no change in competitive intensity; management says it would moderate if competition changes sharply.
Management expects at least double-digit sequential NOV growth in Q2 FY27 and hopes for more, per Rahul Bothra.
Food delivery YoY growth guidance of 18-20% maintained.
Next ~EBITDA breakeven requires about INR30 per order; about INR20 from monetisation (half product margin and mix, half about INR10 from advertising), then another INR25-30 to reach steady EBITDA.
Overall cash breakeven expected within about two quarters, supported by food delivery margin expansion and treasury income; platform innovation funding excluded until PMF and BMF are achieved.
Capital Markets Day / Investor Day scheduled the following week to cover Toing in more detail.
capex_capacity: Plans to open more stores in the same eight existing cities this quarter, more than the number added in the last four quarters.
Some hyper-local stores are capacity-constrained at 2,500-3,000 orders per day, driving the new store additions.
Fixed costs from new stores, including 30-60-90 day ramp costs, are expensed within contribution margin and not capitalised, per management.
demand_pricing: Management says growth will come mainly from transacting user base and frequency rather than AOV, which it is not banking on going forward.
Monetisation (brand take rate, advertising, user fees) drove a large part of the 4-5 quarter improvement to CM breakeven; management says these revenues are sustainable.
Advertising is described as meaningfully kicking in, with inventory and product features being added to the app.
Competition: market has 7-8 players; management sees competitors operating at double-digit negative CM, and expects any new food entrants to target affordability rather than premium.
Toing uses lower commissions than Swiggy so restaurants can offer everyday low prices; management says commission will not be zero in practice.

Instamart delivery-fee line in fully loaded revenue appeared to be zero this quarter versus about INR3 per order previously (analyst observation); management did not confirm and referred to the adjusted revenue walk on page 16.

qa_highlights.question: How should we think about QC strategy: growth at expense of margin or vice versa, and what is the take-rate sustainability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management prioritises growth within a 0 to -100 bps CM band. Take-rate gains come from brand negotiations, advertising and user-fee monetisation, which management says will not reverse.

qa_highlights.question: Is the food delivery zero-commission model a threat?
qa_highlights.answer: Rohit Kapoor argued zero commission is not sustainable; costs must be recovered from restaurants, consumers or delivery partners. Competition is expected in affordability, not premium.

qa_highlights.question: Wage hike and last-mile cost escalation?
qa_highlights.answer: Annual salary revision sits below CM. Minimum wage hikes in some states affect picking and packing; impact described as not material. Last-mile cost rose on seasonal factors including elections and harvest migration; efficiency offset kept the YoY dip to 20 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Are competitors capitalising costs or securitising payables?
qa_highlights.answer: Rahul Bothra said Swiggy does not capitalise employee, tech token or store costs, and is not aware of payables securitisation practices by peers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Instamart growth plan and store expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth from transacting users and frequency; more stores in existing cities as hyper-local stores hit 2,500-3,000 orders/day. Spend priorities are store expansion, speed and serviceability, and selection availability.

qa_highlights.question: Why did platform frequency decline and is private-label conflict with ads a concern?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says it culled low-value MTUs over recent quarters, and QC's lower frequency dilutes the blended metric. Private brands carry higher margins and are experience-driven, so conflict with ads was not seen as material.

risks_watch: Growth-led CM range could drift negative if competitive intensity rises; management says it would moderate the strategy.
Competitors' discounting and funding stress: market has 7-8 players, with several operating at double-digit negative CM.
Toing economics: food monetisation at lower AOV, with delivery partner costs (INR50-60 per order cited by analyst) to be covered; early days.
Reported app rating decline and falling platform frequency raised by analysts; management said it would look into ratings.
Whether 4-week NOV momentum (10%) sustains through the quarter; management described it as hard to predict.
Instamart leadership change (Nandita appointed) and fuller Toing detail due at the Investor Day.
summary.management_tone: Confident on monetisation durability and food delivery margins, but deliberately flexible on quick commerce margin. Management was evasive on Toing unit economics and competitive specifics, deferring detail to the next week's Investor Day.

adds.what: More Instamart dark stores than added in the last four quarters, in the existing eight cities

growth.why: Food delivery YoY growth of 18-20% is maintained for FY27 (about 18% adjusted growth this quarter), and Q2 NOV guided to at least double-digit QoQ growth, backed by store additions in existing cities (more than the last four quarters) and monetisation, though no store counts or capex were quantified.
